newsitem.title: USA: WPS Resources nuclear plant to restart.
newsitem.headline: WPS Resources nuclear plant to restart.

text.p: Wisconsin Public Service Corp said Monday that the Kewaunee Nuclear Power Plant is expected to resume generating electricity this week after repairs to steam generators were completed and approved by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
Wisconsin Public Service is a unit of WPS Resources Corp.
The Kewaunee plant is operated by Wisconsin Public Service, which shares ownership with Wisconsin Power & Light, a unit of WPL Holdings Inc and Madison Gas & Electric Go.

"If everything goes as expected, the plant should be producing power this week and will reach full generating capacity of around 500 megawatts about one week later," Charlie Schrock, plant manager, said in a statement.
The plant has been out of service since September for refueling and repairs to two steam generators.
The generators are powered by heat from the nuclear reactor to make steam, which is used to spin a turbine to make electricity.
Small metal tubes inside the 23-year-old generators have corroded over the years and had to be repaired before the plant could begin operating agin, Wisconsin Public Service said.
Getting the Kewaunee plant back in service will help alleviate some concerns about electricity supplies in Wisconsin this summer.
The next outage for Kewaunee is scheduled for the fall of 1998 for refueling and regular maintenance, as well as further inspections of the steam generator tubes.
